description: Neighbours who fix things together every Saturday - bikes, toasters, fences, friendships. Knowledge is shared, never sold.
name: Repair Café Collective

value_cards.because: Expertise has been used as gatekeeping for too long. The person who teaches ten people to fix bikes has done more than the person who fixed a hundred.
value_cards.care_about: Treating technical skill as something to give away, not hoard — the highest act of skill is creating the conditions where you are no longer needed.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Expert capture — repairs that only one person can do, creating permanent dependency.
value_cards.in_conflict: The learner over the efficiency of the fix.
looks_like: Welcoming complete beginners and giving them the first tool to try
Never making someone feel stupid for not knowing something technical
Writing guides in plain language and leaving them where others will find them
value_cards.never_do: Take over a repair from someone who is learning, just because it's faster.
value_cards.title: Knowledge belongs to whoever needs it

value_cards.because: Every object that gets repaired rather than replaced is a material extracted from the earth, a worker paid to make it, and a landfill site it never fills.
value_cards.care_about: Making the first response to any broken thing a serious attempt to fix it — and building the skills and tools to make that possible.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Repair Café as a feel-good event where the same five people fix things for admiring spectators.
value_cards.in_conflict: The person who leaves knowing how over the person who leaves with a working thing.
looks_like: Bringing the broken thing to the café before looking for a replacement
Documenting the repair so the next person can do it themselves
Teaching repair skills explicitly, not just doing the repair for someone
value_cards.never_do: Fix something without explaining what was broken and why.
value_cards.title: Repair over replace

description: Guardians of heirloom seed diversity. Members save, label and swap seeds so no variety is lost.
name: Seed Keepers Alliance

value_cards.because: The Irish potato famine killed a million people because one crop variety fed a nation. Biodiversity is not aesthetic richness; it is civilisational insurance.
value_cards.care_about: Treating each seed variety as a unique living library — carrying adaptations, stories and potential that cannot be reconstructed once lost.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Seed banks that store seeds nobody is growing. Diversity on paper rather than in the soil.
value_cards.in_conflict: The variety at risk of loss over the one already well-represented.
looks_like: Maintaining at least three independent copies of every variety in the network
Growing-out rare varieties every three years so viability is tested and refreshed
Recording the story and origin of every variety alongside the seeds themselves
value_cards.never_do: Allow a variety to go below minimum viable population without raising the alarm.
value_cards.title: Every variety is irreplaceable

value_cards.because: A seed without the knowledge of how to grow it is an archive without a reading room. The wisdom lives in growers, not databases, and it is equally at risk.
value_cards.care_about: Keeping the accumulated understanding of how to grow each variety — what soil it loves, when it bolts, how it has been used — as inseparable from the seed itself.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Extracting seeds without reciprocity. Treating traditional knowledge as raw material for our records.
value_cards.in_conflict: The source community's access and agency over our archival completeness.
looks_like: Recording grower interviews and stories alongside germination data
Visiting elder growers to learn what hasn't been written down
Returning seeds to communities of origin with the knowledge attached
value_cards.never_do: Take seeds from a community without asking what they need in return.
value_cards.title: Traditional knowledge alongside the seed

description: Stewards of the shared GPU cluster. We allocate compute by need and contribution, decided by the members themselves.
name: Open Compute Guild

value_cards.because: Centralised control of scarce resources without accountability always drifts toward serving the powerful. Transparency is not optional; it is the mechanism.
value_cards.care_about: Making every decision about who gets compute time visible, documented and contestable by any member.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Transparency theatre — publishing decisions after they are made without any genuine input mechanism.
value_cards.in_conflict: The documented process over the trusted judgment of any individual.
looks_like: Publishing the allocation queue and the criteria in full
Holding open monthly reviews where any member can challenge a decision
Recording the reasoning behind each allocation, not just the outcome
value_cards.never_do: Make an allocation decision in a private channel.
value_cards.title: Transparent allocation

value_cards.because: A commons that drifts toward rewarding the already-powerful is not a commons. The allocation method is the values made concrete.
value_cards.care_about: Allocating the shared resource to those with the most valuable questions — not the most resources, the loudest voices, or the longest tenure.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Allocation that consistently rewards the same institutions. A waiting list that only moves for people with connections.
value_cards.in_conflict: The first-time researcher with an excellent question over the repeat user with a mediocre one.
looks_like: Scoring proposals on research quality, not applicant reputation
Weighting contribution history but never letting it dominate over question quality
Maintaining a reserve for unfunded researchers with no existing track record
value_cards.never_do: Allow social relationships to influence allocation without documenting that they did.
value_cards.title: Compute time by need and contribution
